spec.title: Subsystem inventory
spec.description: Every (system, subsystem) tuple seen in range. Surfaces newly-shipped and silently-dropped subsystems.

spec.expr: sum by (system, subsystem) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | system!="" [$__range]))

spec.title: Top error messages
spec.description: Most frequent warn/error events. Top of this list is where to spend the next round of fixes. Errors from third-party loggers (OTLP exporter, requests, etc.) show as "untagged" — fix at source by adding structlog system/subsystem kwargs.

spec.expr: topk(20, sum by (event, system, subsystem) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | label_format system=`{{or .system "untagged"}}`, subsystem=`{{or .subsystem "untagged"}}` | level=~"warning|error" [$__range])))

spec.title: Log rate by system
spec.description: Total log rate aggregated by system.

spec.expr: sum by (system) (rate({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | system!="" [$__interval]))

spec.title: Warn + error rate by system
spec.description: Warn + error rate aggregated by system. First place to look during an incident.

spec.expr: sum by (system) (rate({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | system!="" | level=~"warning|error" [$__interval]))

spec.title: Signup pipeline — recent logs (any system)
spec.description: Live tail of all logs tagged with signup, regardless of system. Useful when tracing a single user click across discord/interaction → events/services → discord/dispatch → discord/celery. Filter by `interaction_id` to follow one click.

spec.expr: {service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | tags_csv=~".*signup.*"

spec.title: Log rate by tags_csv
spec.description: Cross-system view of which tag-clusters are active.

spec.expr: sum by (tags_csv) (rate({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | tags_csv!="" [$__interval]))

spec.title: Internal API errors (4xx warn / 5xx error) by status
spec.description: Rate of internal_http_error from app.internal_client wrappers. 4xx are caller/business errors (e.g. match_unparsed 422); 5xx indicate real backend bugs. Spike in either is page-worthy if sustained.

spec.expr: sum by (http_method, http_status_code) (rate({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | event="internal_http_error" [$__interval]))

spec.title: Internal API unreachable (network errors)
spec.description: Network-layer failures from app.internal_client (timeouts, DNS, connection refused). Any non-zero rate means workers/bot can't reach Daphne — signup writes are degraded.

spec.expr: sum by (error_class, http_method) (rate({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | event="internal_http_network_error" [$__interval]))

spec.title: Internal API errors — recent
spec.description: Tail of internal-API error lines (transport-layer). Inspect body_excerpt / error_class / http_path to triage.

spec.expr: {service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | event=~"internal_http_error|internal_http_network_error"

spec.title: Steam match-store failures by reason
spec.description: reason=match_unparsed is benign (Steam hasn't finished parsing; next sync tick retries). Any other reason (internal_api_unreachable, internal_api_status_*) is a real ingest failure worth surfacing.

spec.expr: sum by (reason) (rate({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | event="steam_match_store_failed" [$__interval]))

spec.title: Signup-post routing warnings (forum/legacy)
spec.description: Data-quality signal for DiscordEventMsgSignup rows: forum_post_missing_thread_id = forum row without a thread_id; legacy_channel_type = row predating the explicit channel_type field. Both fall back to the thread_id-vs-channel_id heuristic. Use to drive a one-time backfill.

spec.expr: {service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | event=~"forum_post_missing_thread_id|legacy_channel_type"

spec.title: Top invalidated classes
spec.description: Which models are evicted most over the selected window. Sudden spike on a single class usually means a write path started cascading too widely.

spec.expr: topk(20, sum by (obj_class) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | event="cache_invalidate" | obj_class!="" [$__range])))

spec.title: Per-row invalidation rate by class
spec.description: `invalidate_obj` rate split by model. Steady-state should track write rate per model; outliers point to N+1 invalidate patterns or accidental cascades.

spec.expr: sum by (obj_class) (rate({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | event="cache_invalidate" | obj_class!="" [$__interval]))

spec.title: Model-wide invalidations (cache_invalidate_model)
spec.description: Full-model eviction events. Should be rare — migrations and the daily avatar bulk path are the only known sources. Spikes here are worth chasing: they cold-start every cached entry for the model, and any hot-read endpoint will hit the DB until the cache warms back up.

spec.expr: sum by (obj_class) (rate({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="" | event="cache_invalidate_model" [$__interval]))

spec.title: Lines that broke `| json` (jsonparsererr)
spec.description: Log lines that Loki's `| json` parser rejects. Source labels (code_file_path, code_function_name, code_line_number) tell you which Python file is emitting broken JSON — usually an f-string containing a stray `{` like a dict literal or repr() output. Fix at source by switching the call to structlog kwargs.

spec.expr: {service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="jsonparsererr"

spec.title: Top sources of broken JSON
spec.description: Which source files are emitting broken JSON, ranked by count. Fix the top entries at source.

spec.expr: topk(20, sum by (code_file_path, code_function_name, code_line_number) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment=~"$env"} | json | __error__="jsonparsererr" [$__range])))

DraftForge structured-log dashboard. Overview row at the top summarizes inventory, log rate, warn/error rate, and top error events. Each system in the canonical taxonomy gets its own collapsed row below — expand the one you care about. Bottom row surfaces lines that fail `| json` parsing so we can fix them at source. See .claude/skills/logging/SKILL.md for the taxonomy.
